narrative: Material PL3__MDAB776E exhibits moderately variable daily demand (CV=39%) with a significant zero-demand fraction (~21% of working days), consistent with intermittent-to-regular demand. Lead times are highly variable (CV=76%), which is the primary driver of safety stock requirements. The current SAP policy carries zero safety stock, structurally exposing the material to stockouts under the 95% service level target. An (r,Q) fixed-order-quantity policy is recommended with SS=712, ROP=1504, and OQ=5248 — the order quantity is storage-capped from the unconstrained EOQ of 13,475, which binds the capacity constraint exactly.
warnings: Storage capacity constraint is binding: unconstrained EOQ=13475 capped to OQ=5248 (max_storage_units=5960.672, safety_stock=712).

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is moderately variable but not severely intermittent (non-zero fraction=79%), and lead times are observable with sufficient observations for parametric sigma_LTD estimation. The (r,Q) policy is the classical fit: trigger a fixed replenishment of Q units whenever inventory falls to the reorder point r, combining EOQ cost efficiency with a safety buffer sized to the 95th percentile of lead-time demand. The MOQ=1370 is comfortably below the capacity-capped OQ=5248, so no MOQ conflict exists.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The storage cap of 5,960.672 units binds tightly: SS+OQ=5,960 leaves only 0.672 units of headroom. Any upward revision to safety stock (e.g., due to higher demand volatility or worse lead-time performance) will require either a reduction in OQ or a storage capacity increase. Annual ordering cost rises to $1,050 vs. the unconstrained EOQ optimum of ~$518, representing a $532/year capacity-induced penalty.
